**Why a geometric quotient is categorical.** Let $\pi:X\to Y$ satisfy (i)–(iii)
and let $f:X\to Z$ be a $G$-invariant morphism to a classical variety $Z$. By
(i) two points of a fibre of $\pi$ lie in one orbit, on which $f$ is constant,
so $f$ factors through a unique set map $\bar f:Y\to Z$. For $W\subseteq Z$
open, $\pi^{-1}(\bar f^{-1}(W))=f^{-1}(W)$ is open in $X$ by continuity of $f$,
so $\bar f^{-1}(W)$ is open in $Y$ by (ii): $\bar f$ is continuous. If $V$ is an
affine chart of $Z$ with coordinates $s$ and $U:=\bar f^{-1}(V)$, then
$s\circ f$ is a $G$-invariant regular function on $\pi^{-1}(U)$, hence by (iii)
is the pullback along $\pi$ of a unique regular function on $U$; that function
is $s\circ\bar f$. Since this holds for every coordinate $s$ of an affine chart,
$\bar f$ is a morphism
([[def-classical-affine-variety-morphism]],
[[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), and local
agreement of the resulting morphisms on overlapping charts gives a morphism
$Y\to Z$. Surjectivity in (i) makes the factorisation unique. If also
$\pi':X\to Y'$ is a categorical quotient, the universal property applied to
$\pi'$ and to $\pi$ yields morphisms $\varphi:Y\to Y'$ with $\varphi\pi=\pi'$
and $\psi:Y'\to Y$ with $\psi\pi'=\pi$; then $(\varphi\psi)\pi'=\pi'$ and
$(\psi\varphi)\pi=\pi$, so uniqueness of the factorisation of $\pi'$ through
$\pi'$ and of $\pi$ through $\pi$ forces $\varphi\psi=\operatorname{id}_{Y'}$
and $\psi\varphi=\operatorname{id}_Y$. Thus categorical and geometric
quotients are unique up to unique isomorphism, and for a geometric quotient
(i)–(ii) say exactly that the underlying map is the quotient map of the orbit
equivalence relation with the quotient topology.

For $k>0$, a word frame $C(x)$ is a matrix whose columns are $k$ fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard framing basis vectors. The opens $U_C=\{x:\det C(x)\ne0\}$ cover $X$; words of length at most $k-1$ suffice. Each slice $S_C=\{x\in U_C:C(x)=I_V\}$ gives quotient coordinates, with $GL(V)\times S_C\to U_C$ a biholomorphism. Slice changes are holomorphic, in fact given by matrix inversion and polynomial operations on their domains. The quotient is also a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite $T$-invariant affine atlas of these slices, and the map from $X$ is a geometric quotient in the regular-function sense.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and $n\ge0$, let
$S=k[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be graded by total degree with $\deg x_i=1$, let
$\mathbb P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}S$ with twisting sheaves
$\mathcal O(d)=\widetilde{S(d)}$, and let $F$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_k}$-module. Then there is a finitely generated graded
$S$-module $M$ with $\widetilde M\cong F$ and an exact sequence of graded
$S$-modules with degree-preserving maps
$$0\longrightarrow F_{n+1}\longrightarrow F_n\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow F_0\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow 0$$
in which every $F_i$ is a finite direct sum of shifted free modules $S(d)$
with $d\in\mathbb Z$, and whose sheafification
$$0\longrightarrow\widetilde F_{n+1}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\widetilde F_0\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow 0$$
is an exact sequence of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^n_k}$-modules in which every
$\widetilde F_i$ is a finite direct sum $\bigoplus_j\mathcal O(d_{ij})$ of
twisting sheaves. The resolution has length at most $n+1$: the displayed free
terms $F_0,\dots,F_{n+1}$ are finite direct sums of shifted free modules, any
of them may be zero, a shorter resolution is allowed when it terminates
earlier, and the truncation degree of $M$ is chosen so that $M$ is finitely
generated and $\widetilde M\cong F$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring with $1$,
let $X$ be a scheme projective over $A$ in the finite-dimensional
H-projective convention ([[def-projective-morphism-pre-proj]]): the structure
morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ factors as a closed immersion
$X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N_A$ followed by the projection, for some $N\ge0$
([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]]). Let $L$ be an ample
invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-ample-invertible-sheaf]],
[[def-invertible-sheaf]]) and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent
$\mathcal O_X$-module ([[def-coherent-module-scheme]]). Then there is an
integer $m_0$ such that
$$H^q\bigl(X,\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L^{\otimes m}\bigr)=0$$
for every $q>0$ and every integer $m\ge m_0$, with a single bound $m_0$
working simultaneously for all $q$; here $H^q$ is sheaf cohomology
([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]) and $L^{\otimes m}$ is the
$m$-fold tensor power ([[def-twist-quasi-coherent-sheaf-projective]]). The
empty scheme $X$, the empty base $\operatorname{Spec}A=\varnothing$, the zero
ring $A=0$, the zero module $\mathcal F=0$ and the case of an ample $L$ with
$\mathcal O(1)$ already very ample for a power $L^{\otimes d}$ with $d=1$ are
included. No effectivity of $m_0$ is claimed.

citations.quote: For $n=2$ or $3$, let $X=\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}$ and let $X^{an}$ be its complex analytic space. Define analytification by $\mathcal F^{an}=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_{X^{an}}$. It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from algebraic coherent sheaves (locally finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-modules) to holomorphic coherent sheaves. It identifies algebraic and holomorphic morphisms, preserves cohomology and the derived morphism groups $\operatorname{Ext}^q$, and commutes with restriction to the fixed hyperplane $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}$. For an algebraic coherent sheaf $\mathcal E$ flat over a finite-type complex parameter scheme $S$, let $p:X\times S\to S$ be projection. Analytification commutes with the algebraic family structure and fiber restrictions. Whenever the algebraic and analytic higher direct images $R^qp_*\mathcal E$ are locally free and the natural maps from their residue-field fibers to $H^q(X_s,\mathcal E_s)$ are isomorphisms, the comparison identifies those direct images and base-change maps. No assertion is made that an arbitrary holomorphic family over a nonproper algebraic base algebraizes.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the finite
coherent-resolution and cohomological suppliers. A section $s$ of a rank-$d$
bundle $Q$ is a **regular section** here if, at each point of its zero scheme
$Z(s)$, some local frame expresses $s$ by $d$ components forming a regular
sequence of length $d$ in the local ring. Under this hypothesis it has exact
Koszul resolution
$\bigwedge^dQ^\vee\to\cdots\to Q^\vee\to\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{Z(s)}\to0$.
Tensoring with a vector bundle preserves it. If a coherent sheaf $H$ has a
finite locally free resolution on a scheme and $t$ is a Cartier equation acting
injectively on $H$, restricting the resolution to $t=0$ remains exact and
resolves $H/tH$. In the deformation blowup for a closed embedding of smooth
quasi-projective varieties $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$, let $E$ be a finite
locally free sheaf on $X$. The strict transform
$F:X\times\mathbb P^1\hookrightarrow M$ is disjoint from
$B=\operatorname{Bl}_XY$, and a resolution of $F_*\operatorname{pr}_X^*E$
restricts exactly to the ordinary $Y$ fibre and to
$P=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{lines}}(N\oplus1)$; on $B$ it is an exact complex.

citations.quote: These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

derivations.claim: There is exactly one linear map between any of the zero spaces, so $B_1,B_2,I,J$ are all zero maps. The complex and real equations are equalities between zero endomorphisms. The span of the empty family is $0=V$, and no nonzero subspace of $V$ exists; hence stability and costability hold. The gauge groups have one element, so each quotient consists of one point.

Substituting $V=0$ into the monad leaves $0\to W\mathcal O\to0$. Its kernel at the right is $W\mathcal O$ and the image at the left is zero, so the middle cohomology is canonically $W\mathcal O$. Restriction to $L_\infty$ is the identity framing on the prescribed basis of $W$. Since $\chi(\mathcal O(m))=\binom{m+2}{2}$, its Hilbert polynomial is $N\binom{m+2}{2}$, the case $k=0$ of [F2].
